themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 23 complaints last week versus a baseline of 1.9 per week—a 1,127% increase (z-score: 13.75)—suggesting a new operational or enforcement issue emerged this week in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 23 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
No prior news mentions or community board discussion of this issue
reporting_angles: Interview Uber/Lyft drivers and residents about what triggered the sudden surge—illegal parking, congestion, safety incidents?
Check NYPD and TLC enforcement data for any recent crackdowns or changes in ride-sharing operations in the district

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 20 this week versus a baseline of 3.6 per week—a 452% increase (z-score: 7.73)—indicating rapid deterioration or concentrated damage across the neighborhood this week.
evidence: 20 sidewalk condition complaints this week vs. 3.6 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Community board budget requests include infrastructure upgrades, suggesting chronic street maintenance issues
reporting_angles: Map this week's 20 complaints geographically—are they concentrated on a few blocks or distributed?
Investigate whether recent weather, construction, or infrastructure work triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Street Encampment Jump
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 10 this week from a baseline of 1.1 per week—a 789% increase (z-score: 5.49)—suggesting a visible homelessness crisis emerging or concentrating in the district this week.
evidence: 10 encampment complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Community board requests repeatedly mention park safety and security staff—signals long-standing but potentially worsening issue
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners about where encampments are concentrated and what prompted the surge
Examine city's outreach and shelter capacity response—is there a systemic failure or external driver (weather, policy change, closure)?

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded to 3 this week from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—indicating a new enforcement issue, unlicensed operation, or health/sanitation concern this week.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Community board budget requests include litter collection—may signal sanitation issues near food vendors
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints relate to unlicensed vendors, health code violations, or parking/congestion from carts
Check Department of Health and Parks Enforcement violation records for this week and prior week

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 4 last week from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 967% increase (z-score: 5.21)—signaling possible storm damage, disease, or neglect in the district's canopy last week.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Community board budget requests include park reconstruction and upgrade—suggests ongoing environmental maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Check NYC Parks Department records for disease, pests, or storm damage affecting Washington Heights/Inwood canopy
Interview Parks & Recreation staff about tree maintenance backlog and replanting timelines
